ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the intersection point of the lines $y=-x+a$ and $y=x+b$ has an abscissa of $-2$, and the abscissas of the points where the two lines intersect the $x$-axis are $-1$ and $-3$, respectively. What is the solution set of the inequality $-x+a > x+b > 0$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let us assume that the intersection point of the line $y = -x + a$ and the line $y = x + b$ has an abscissa of $-2$. The abscissas where the two lines intersect the x-axis are $-1$ and $-3$, respectively.\\
Therefore, the solution set of the inequality in $x$, $-x + a > x + b > 0$, corresponds to the range of $x$ values for which the line $y = -x + a$ is above the line $y = x + b$, i.e., $-3 < x < -2$.\\
Hence, the solution set is $x \in \boxed{(-3, -2)}$.
